office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Alex Zimmerman
incumbent.summary: Alex Zimmerman, a North Vernon attorney, has represented House District 67 since July 2023, when a Republican caucus chose him to fill the seat left by Rep. Randy Frye; he was elected unopposed in 2024 [3, 4, 5]. He is vice chair of the House Judiciary Committee [3].
record: Committees: Judiciary (vice chair), Courts and Criminal Code, and Rules and Legislative Procedures, according to his caucus biography [3].

2024: Authored two amendments, which failed, that would have barred federal funding for INDOT's Link 101 Corridor highway project and required the agency to consider improving existing roads first; when INDOT canceled the project on May 1, 2024, he said constituents had raised concerns about farmland and "generational homesteads" [6].

2025: Authored HEA 1114, which makes driving without ever having obtained a license a Level 5 or 6 felony when it causes bodily injury, catastrophic injury or death; he said he wrote it after a Holton man was killed in a head-on crash with an unlicensed driver [7, 8]. Also authored HEA 1014, which caps total incarceration for consecutive misdemeanor sentences, and HEA 1079; all three were ceremonially signed by Gov. Mike Braun [8].

2026: House sponsor of SEA 285, which prohibits unauthorized camping or sleeping in public spaces and requires police to give first-time offenders a warning and help with shelter and services before issuing a citation; Zimmerman called it "a balanced approach" [9].

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) [10]; the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) [11]; and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) [12].

race_context: House District 67 covers portions of Decatur, Jefferson, Jennings and Ripley counties in southeast Indiana, according to the House Republican caucus [3]. (It does not include Dearborn or Franklin counties.)
Zimmerman was appointed by a Republican caucus in July 2023 after Rep. Randy Frye resigned, and was elected without opposition in 2024 [4, 5].
Both candidates were the only filers in their party's May 5, 2026 primary [5, 13].
No debate or candidate forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent Republican and North Vernon attorney seeking his second full term [3, 5].
background: Attorney with a private law practice in North Vernon; earned his law degree from the IU Robert H. McKinney School of Law [3].
Previously worked for the Indiana Senate as a legislative assistant, majority legal associate and deputy majority attorney [3].
path_to_ballot: Filed for reelection and was the only Republican in the May 5, 2026 primary [13, 5].

items: Says HEA 1114 is meant as "a deterrent to ensure those who do not have a license refrain from getting behind the wheel" [7].
On SEA 285 (2026), said the law prioritizes "intervention and support" for people experiencing homelessness, "with any potential enforcement action as a last resort" [9].
Opposed INDOT's proposed Link 101 Corridor through Ripley and neighboring counties and welcomed its cancellation in 2024 [6].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No public statements about his opponent were found.
plans: His campaign website lists priorities including the Second Amendment, banning China and other foreign adversaries from buying farmland, election security, parents' rights and bringing jobs to southern Indiana; the site still refers to the November 5 (2024) election date [14].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: Campaign website appears not to have been updated for 2026.
Content of HEA 1079 was not verified.
No campaign-finance totals were checked on the Indiana campaign finance portal.

candidates.summary: Democratic nominee; very little public information about his background or positions was found [13].
background: No verified background information was found.
path_to_ballot: Filed in Jennings County as a Democratic candidate for House District 67 and was the only Democrat listed in the May 5, 2026 primary [13, 5].
on_incumbent: No statements about the incumbent were found.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were found.
gaps: Unverified: a BallotReady profile lists a 2014 bachelor's degree in music education from the University of Indianapolis.
No campaign website, social media page, news interview or questionnaire response was found; iVoterGuide rates him as having insufficient information.
